question: Is Westpac's targeted FY26 productivity enough to restore positive jaws, or is it mainly an offset to continuing wage, banker and UNITE investment pressure? Ground the judgment in the FY25 expense bridge, the investment-spend mix and the disclosed duration/expensing profile of UNITE.
answer:
**Direct answer.** On the FY25 evidence, Westpac's targeted FY26 productivity (>$500m) reads mainly as an offset to continuing wage, banker and UNITE investment pressure, not as a route back to positive jaws. The FY25 bridge shows productivity (−$402m) recovering under a third of the +$1,374m gross cost build, and FY26 guidance re-arms every driver while UNITE's expensed spend keeps rising into FY29.

**FY25 expense bridge (FY24 $10,944m → FY25 $11,916m, +9%).** Staff costs +$397m (salary and EBA increases, superannuation, investment in bankers), technology +$146m, volume & other +$199m, investments +$359m (UNITE investment $399m; amortisation up $106m), restructuring charge +$273m — against productivity of only −$402m (sums of printed bars). Ex-restructuring expenses grew 6% while net operating income grew 3% (statutory): negative jaws of ~3ppt; on the ex-notable-items basis the cost-to-income ratio rose to 53.0% from 50.3%, and pre-provision profit fell 3% to $10,548m. 2H25 repeats the shape: productivity −$249m vs investments +$208m, staff +$143m, restructuring +$273m.

**Investment-spend mix.** FY25 spend was $1,918m (+9%): UNITE $660m (34% of spend, 74% expensed), growth & productivity $563m (30%), risk & regulatory $695m (36%). FY26 guidance: total ~$2bn with UNITE up to $850–950m at ~75% expensed — lifting expensed UNITE from ~$488m to ~$640–710m (my arithmetic) — partly offset by expected reductions in growth & productivity and risk & regulation spend and a moderating amortisation increase ($889m → $995m in FY25).

**UNITE duration/expensing.** The plan "extends into FY29"; UNITE is c.40% of total investment spend in FY27–FY28 with lower spend in FY29, and c.75% of spend is expensed. Benefits land only "after the initiative is complete", and disclosed completed-initiative savings are small (~$5m and ~$4m annual savings on $7m/$5m costs). Westpac frames UNITE as closing its cost-to-income gap to peers — a multi-year ambition, not FY26 jaws.

**Arithmetic.** >$500m of targeted productivity against EBA +3–4% on $6,326m staff costs, more bankers, ~$150–225m more expensed UNITE and still-rising amortisation leaves expense growth plausibly near FY25's 6% ex-restructuring pace; positive jaws would need revenue growth well above that, and no FY26 revenue guidance is disclosed.

**Not settled.** No explicit jaws target, no total UNITE benefit pool, no split of the >$500m between Fit for Growth and other productivity; every FY26 figure here is a target printed in FY25 documents — the corpus holds no FY26 WBC document.

key_facts.fact: FY25 operating expenses were $11,916m, up 9% from $10,944m in FY24; excluding the $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge they rose 6%.

The FY25 expense bridge (FY24 $10,944m to FY25 $11,916m) shows staff costs +$397m, technology +$146m, volume & other +$199m, investments +$359m (UNITE $399m, amortisation +$106m), restructuring +$273m, productivity −$402m.
FY25 net operating income rose 3% to $22,464m while pre-provision profit fell 3% to $10,548m (statutory, FY25 vs FY24).
The expense-to-income ratio excluding Notable Items was 53.0% in FY25, up from 50.3% in FY24.
The 2H25 expense bridge (1H25 $5,698m to 2H25 $6,218m) shows productivity −$249m against investments +$208m, staff +$143m and restructuring +$273m.
FY25 investment spend was $1,918m (+9%): UNITE $660m with 74% expensed (34% of spend), growth & productivity $563m (30%), risk & regulatory $695m (36%).

FY26 guidance: total investment spend ~$2bn, UNITE spend up to $850–950m at ~75% expensed, reductions expected in growth & productivity and risk & regulation spend, and the amortisation increase to moderate.
Fit for Growth benefits are to contribute to targeted productivity of >$500m in FY26.
FY26 cost pressures include an EBA increase of 3% to 4% and continued investment in bankers.
The UNITE plan extends into FY29, with FY26 investment of $850–950m, c.40% of total investment spend in FY27–FY28, lower spend in FY29, and c.75% of spend expensed.
UNITE benefits are expected only after an initiative completes; disclosed FY25 completed initiatives show ~$5m and ~$4m annual cost savings on $7m and $5m initiative costs.
FY25 staff expenses rose 7% to $6,326m mainly due to wage growth, UNITE and investment in bankers; average FTE rose 1% as UNITE/banker hiring more than offset productivity reductions.
Westpac frames UNITE simplification as playing a key role in reducing its cost base and closing its cost-to-income gap relative to peers.

limitations: The corpus holds no WBC document for FY26; this answer was researched in FY25 instead.
The corpus holds no WBC FY26 document; every FY26 figure cited is a forward-looking target or 'key consideration' printed in the FY25 results materials, not an outcome.

The bank discloses no explicit FY26 jaws, revenue-growth or expense-growth guidance; the 'mainly an offset' judgment is inferred from the printed FY25 bridge and FY26 guidance arithmetic, not stated by the bank.

The >$500m is a target ('targeted productivity'); the documents do not disclose the total UNITE benefit pool, the in-year phasing of the >$500m, or the split between Fit for Growth and other productivity sources.
The +$1,374m gross cost build, the ~29% productivity offset ratio, and the expensed-UNITE increase (~$488m to ~$640–710m, ~$150–225m) are my arithmetic on printed figures, not printed line items.
The 53.0% cost-to-income ratio is ex-Notable Items (non-AAS management basis); the 3% revenue growth is statutory net operating income — the jaws comparison follows the bank's own mixed presentation.
UNITE's $399m bridge bar (P&L expense impact) and the 74%-expensed $660m investment spend are different cuts; the FY26 expensed-UNITE comparison uses the investment-spend basis.
